newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission still working on postal notice.
newsitem.headline: Commission still working on postal notice.

text.p: The European Commission's competition directorate-general (DG IV) is still working on a long-awaited notice outlining how the Commission will apply EU competition rules to the postal sector, a DG IV official said on Thursday.
He said he could not predict when the text would go to the full Commission for adoption.
EU Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said last December he expected the notice to be finalised at the start of 1997.

The Commission published a draft of the text in 1995, but held off formally adopting it to give the Telecommunications Council time to agree a related directive, COM(95)227, setting out a plan for opening the EU postal sector to competition.

The Telecommunications Council finally agreed a common position in December. The ministers, under heavy pressure from France, decided to delay any significant liberalisation until at least January 1, 2003.
They set that as a target date for ending state monopolies over direct mail and cross-border mail, agreeing to take a formal decision before the start of 2000.
The Commission had wanted to open up those sectors by the start of 2001 and its draft notice had included that deadline. The new notice will take account of the Council's common position.
The Commission does not plan to delay action until the Council and European Parliament adopt a final decision, however, the DG IV official said.

Private competitors including express and direct mail operators are eagerly awaiting the Commission's notice because it will address issues such as cross-subsidies -- money earned from monopoly services that post offices use to subsidise services open to competition.
However, the European Parliament has demanded that the Commission withdraw the notice, arguing that such unilateral action is inappropriate. Van Miert has refused.
